title: Answer: no account of what life is, and consciousness is not tied to being alive

statements.text: Integrated information theory takes no position on what life is. Its postulates apply to any system of units in a state, living or not, so consciousness is not tied to life. Members of Tononi's group have applied the theory's causal analysis to a model of the yeast cell cycle and suggested that features such as intrinsic control and stable causal borders may help to tell life from non-life, which they treat as autonomy, the power of a living entity to regulate its own internal state. That paper frames this as a proposal for the origin of life problem, not as a definition the theory holds.
statements.scope: IIT 4.0 (2022) and the paper How causal analysis can reveal autonomy in models of biological systems (2017)

sources.quote: In principle, the postulates can be applied to any system of units in a state to determine whether it is conscious, to what degree, and in what way.
